newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Philippines bond/FRN BB, outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Philippines bond/FRN BB, outlook positive.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it assigned its BB rating to the Republic of the Philippines' forthcoming fixed-rate bonds due 2016 and floating-rate bonds due 2011.
"The rating outlook is positive," S&P said in a statement.

"Political support for the government's economic policies should allow the passage of key tax reforms proposed by the government under its Comprehensive Tax Reform programme, over the medium term. However, opposition from powerful vested interests and weakened cooperation between the Ramos Administration and Congress could still result in a dilution of the government's proposals and slippage in the implementation of other reforms crucial to fiscal consolidation," S&P said.

"Improvements in creditworthiness hinge on the enactment of a meaningful tax reform package, which should provide the foundation for a sustained rise in recurrent revenues and allow steady increments in public investment," it said.

S&P also expected creditworthiness to be enhanced by the more cautious monetary policy evident since last year, which should cut inflation to single-digit levels, and by the improved external flexibility resulting from gradually rising levels of domestic saving and foreign direct investment.

"At least $200 million of new fixed-rate bonds and $200 million of new floating-rate bonds may be issued in exchange for outstanding Philippine Brady bonds, also rated BB. Interest reduction bonds due 2017 and 2018 are eligible for exchange," S&P said.
It said the new bonds would be priced on September 23, 1996, and the aggregate amount to be issued would be determined on October 1, 1996.

"Unlike the Brady bonds eligible for the exchange, which are secured as to principal by U.S. Treasury zero-coupon bonds and partly secured as to interest by other high-grade securities, the new bonds will not be collateralized," S&P said.
The foreign currency credit rating on the Republic of the Philippines is BB.
The rating on the Philippines is based on the following.
-- The progressive liberalization of its economy.
S&P said the rating remains constrained by the following.
-- Low savings and investment rates of 19 percent and 22 percent of GDP, respectively, which constrain economic performance relative to its neighbours.
-- The vulnerability of the balance of payments.
